claims.text: The study addresses learning to defer to multiple experts when a predictor trained with a standard classification loss is already available and joint retraining could be prohibitively costly.
The approach first trains a predictor with a standard surrogate such as logistic loss, then learns a deferral function while keeping the predictor's scoring function fixed.

In the score-based setting, the second-stage surrogate combines a classification-surrogate term weighted by predictor correctness with expert terms weighted by one minus each expert's deferral cost; the retained-predictor score is its maximum class score.
The predictor-rejector formulation learns a separate deferral function and represents the retained predictor by a fixed zero score and each expert by the negative of its rejector score.

Experiments used CIFAR-10 and SVHN, ResNet-4 predictor and deferral models, and ResNet-10, ResNet-16 and ResNet-28 experts. Training used Adam, batch size 128, weight decay 1×10−4, 15 epochs for SVHN and 50 for CIFAR-10, with no data augmentation.

Under the required consistency bounds for each stage, the paper establishes hypothesis-set-specific bounds relating deferral regret to both stages' surrogate regrets and minimizability gaps; the resulting surrogate families are Bayes-consistent.

For logistic losses in both stages, constant expert costs c_j(x,y)=β_j and hypothesis sets closed under scaling, the paper establishes realizable consistency in both formulations, subject to the minimizer conditions stated in Theorems 5 and 7.

Without base costs, overall accuracy for one, two and three experts was respectively 91.85±0.01%, 92.77±0.02% and 93.30±0.02% on SVHN, and 72.63±0.20%, 75.84±0.35% and 77.68±0.07% on CIFAR-10; values are means±standard deviations over three runs.

With base costs, overall accuracy for one, two and three experts was respectively 91.66±0.01%, 92.05±0.10% and 92.19±0.03% on SVHN, and 71.73±0.06%, 72.31±0.31% and 72.42±0.12% on CIFAR-10, over three runs. Expert base costs were 0.1, 0.12 and 0.14 for SVHN and 0.3, 0.32 and 0.34 for CIFAR-10.
The deferral cost function is typically selected through cross-validation; a principled method for choosing it remains future work.
The authors report being unaware of established baselines for their two-stage deferral setting.
The paper introduces families of two-stage surrogate losses for both score-based and predictor-rejector learning to defer with multiple experts.

As an additional theoretical contribution, the paper derives multiclass H-consistency bounds with one fixed scoring function, assuming the underlying hypothesis set is symmetric and complete, using a softmax-based proof construction.
